In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Oetztal basement has been formed in a pre-Riphean period, that is to say, more than 1.200 m. y. old.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Oetztal basement has a pre-Riphean (more than 1200 m. y.) age.
the Ötztal crystalline basement has undergone a pre-alpine evolution with four phases: folding, metamorphism (except eclogite), migmatization, intrusion.

the Ötztal crystalline basement has been subjected to pre-alpine polyphase evolution with regard to folding (flow folding), metamorphism (high-grade and medium-grade), migmatization, intrusions (granites, pegmatites, gneisses), and eclogite formation (Fig. 1).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Oetztal Crystalline Basement (OCB) is not a single, homogeneous body but rather a composite of several distinct rock units, which were amalgamated during a complex pre-riphaeic history.
the Oetztal Crystalline Basement is a part of the pre-Ripehan basement of the Eastern Alps.
the high-pressure rocks of the Austroalpine Unit are part of a large-scale nappe stack that is rooted in the lower crust and that is composed of different units that were exhumed at different times.
